description: Pins transport-failure classification across the CLI/MCP boundary: cli/schist/sync.py `_is_network_error` and mcp-server/src/tools.ts `classifyPushFailure` (its TRANSPORT_PATTERNS / TRANSPORT_SHAPE_RES branch). The two lists were hand-maintained and diverged in BOTH directions (#594 #601 #604 #605 #606): seven phrasings the CLI knew were absent from MCP, four MCP knew were absent from the CLI, and `unable to access` survived in MCP after #592 removed it from the CLI as an HTTP-auth false positive. Every case here is asserted against BOTH implementations, so a phrasing added to one side and not the other fails CI. Consumed by cli/tests/test_sync.py and mcp-server/tests/transport-classification-parity.test.ts.
notes: `network` is the CLI's _is_network_error verdict. `mcp_class` is the class classifyPushFailure must return; null means this case is not asserted against MCP, with `mcp_skip_why` saying why.

Wrapper timeout banners (PULL/PUSH_NO_RESPONSE_PREFIX) are deliberately absent: the CLI matches them on its own producer token at line start, while MCP learns of a spawn timeout from outcome.timedOut rather than from text. Pinning a text verdict for those would encode a contract neither side actually implements.

Negative cases named steer-* are the discriminating half. The hub echoes offending FILEPATHS into its output and git relays local failures with paths attached, so every phrasing added here must be matched in a shape that a vault filename cannot forge (#535/#584). Each newly added matcher has a steer-* twin.

Two altitudes, deliberately. `network` is the bare _is_network_error predicate; `mcp_class` is MCP's whole classifyPushFailure. So a case can honestly carry network=true with a non-transport mcp_class: the predicate matches and an earlier branch wins. The CLI is asserted at MCP's altitude through classify_push_failure, whose expected value is DERIVED from mcp_class rather than stored per case — a stored copy would be duplicated data free to drift from the class it has to agree with (#617).

order-* cases are the ordering half, as steer-* is the anchoring half. A steer-* case proves a vault filename cannot make a matcher fire at all; an order-* case covers the shapes where a matcher DOES fire on vault-controlled text and only branch order keeps the verdict right. Every network marker needs both twins.

cases.name: dns-ssh-temporary-failure
cases.input: ssh: Could not resolve hostname schist-hub: Temporary failure in name resolution
cases.why: ssh + getaddrinfo phrasing; MCP had only the narrower 'could not resolve hostname'

cases.name: dns-curl-could-not-resolve-host
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi.local/vault.git/': Could not resolve host: pi.local
cases.why: curl says 'host', ssh says 'hostname' — the shared prefix is 'could not resolve'

cases.name: connect-refused
cases.input:
ssh: connect to host pi.local port 22: Connection refused
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
cases.why: the phrasing the bare 'connection' marker used to cover

cases.name: connect-operation-timed-out
cases.input: ssh: connect to host pi.local port 22: Operation timed out
cases.why: ssh's own timeout line, distinct from our wrapper banner

cases.name: connect-connection-timed-out
cases.input: ssh: connect to host pi port 22: Connection timed out
cases.why: the other timeout phrasing

cases.name: connect-curl-failed-to-connect-no-route
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi.local/vault.git/': Failed to connect to pi.local port 443: No route to host
cases.why: curl error 7; MCP had neither 'failed to connect' nor the pairing

cases.name: connect-curl-couldnt-connect
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi/v.git/': curl: (7) couldn't connect to host
cases.why: curl error 7 alternate phrasing; had no CLI test case either (#600)

cases.name: connect-network-unreachable
cases.input: ssh: connect to host pi port 22: Network is unreachable
cases.why: ENETUNREACH

cases.name: connect-closed-by-remote-host
cases.input:
Connection closed by remote host
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
cases.why: MCP had only 'connection closed by remote host'; CLI's 'connection closed' is broader

cases.name: midxfer-curl-recv-failure
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi/v.git/': Recv failure: Connection reset by peer
cases.why: curl error 56; added to the CLI by #592, never to MCP (#604)

cases.name: midxfer-curl-send-failure
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi.local/vault.git/': Send failure: Connection reset by peer
cases.why: curl error 55; #592 added it to the CLI with no test (#600) and not to MCP (#604)

cases.name: midxfer-curl-empty-reply
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi.local/vault.git/': Empty reply from server
cases.why: curl error 52; same gap as above (#600/#604)

cases.name: midxfer-git-write-error-broken-pipe
cases.input: fatal: write error: Broken pipe
cases.why: git's pack-write drop; MCP had bare 'broken pipe', CLI had nothing (#605)

cases.name: midxfer-ssh-packet-write-wait
cases.input:
packet_write_wait: Connection to pi.local port 22: Broken pipe
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
cases.why: OpenSSH 7.7+ mid-transfer drop. Says 'Connection to', not 'connect to host', so the old _NETWORK_CONNECT_RE missed it (#601)

cases.name: midxfer-git-remote-end-hung-up
cases.input: fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly
cases.why: MCP had it, CLI did not (#605)

cases.name: midxfer-git-early-eof
cases.input:
fatal: early EOF
fatal: index-pack failed
cases.why: remote closed before the full pack; MCP had it, CLI did not (#606)

cases.name: kex-connection-closed
cases.input: kex_exchange_identification: Connection closed by remote host
cases.why: #606 cited this as misclassified; it already passed via 'connection closed'. Kept to pin that it stays classified whichever tail ssh chooses

cases.name: kex-banner-exchange-invalid-format
cases.input: kex_exchange_identification: banner exchange: Connection to 10.0.0.2 port 22: invalid format
cases.why: the tail #606 was actually right about: no existing marker matched this one

cases.name: kex-invalid-protocol-identifier
cases.input: kex_exchange_identification: server sent invalid protocol identifier
cases.why: fail2ban/LB closing before negotiation; no existing marker matched

cases.name: refusal-http-403
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi.local/vault.git/': The requested URL returned error: 403
cases.why: git stamps 'unable to access' on 401/403/404 as readily as on a dead socket — the #594 false positive

cases.name: refusal-http-401
cases.input: fatal: unable to access 'https://pi.local/vault.git/': The requested URL returned error: 401
cases.why: same wrapper, same reason

cases.name: refusal-hub-acl
cases.input:
remote: REJECTED: push contains out-of-scope writes
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined)
cases.why: a refusal about our content, never a transport blip

cases.name: app-connection-rejected
cases.input: Error: repository connection rejected (authentication required)
cases.why: contains 'connection' but is an auth answer

cases.name: app-jump-host-policy
cases.input: connection to jump host blocked by security policy
cases.why: #584's original report

cases.name: app-request-timed-out
cases.input: request timed out after 30s
cases.why: contains 'timed out' but is not a transport failure

cases.name: local-invalid-refspec
cases.input: fatal: invalid refspec ''
cases.why: #321: a bare `fatal:` is not network evidence

cases.name: midxfer-ssh-packet-write-host-is-down
cases.input:
packet_write_wait: Connection to 10.0.0.5 port 22: Host is down
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
cases.why: OpenSSH formats this as 'Connection to %s port %d: %s' with a raw strerror tail, so the tail set is every socket errno — EHOSTDOWN here. No marker covers 'host is down', which makes this the case that the connect-SHAPE matcher exists for: without it the only packet_write_wait tails classified are the ones that happen to collide with a marker (#601)

cases.why: the original #584 filename, which satisfied all three pre-#592 loose markers

cases.name: steer-conflict-port-22-filename
cases.input: CONFLICT (content): Merge conflict in notes/port-22-notes.md
cases.why: pins that the ssh port SHAPE, not a bare \bport\b, is what matches

cases.name: steer-local-rebase-echoes-could-not-resolve
cases.input:
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by rebase:
	notes/could not resolve.md
Please commit your changes or stash them before you rebase.
cases.why: a LOCAL failure echoing a vault path containing 'could not resolve'. The phrase arrives as DATA on a line no transport producer wrote, so it must not classify — reporting 'Hub unreachable' for a dirty worktree sends the user to the wrong layer, and is #584's defect pointing the worse way. One case per marker: a marker whose anchoring is untested is a marker that will be narrowed wrong later (#601/#604/#605/#606 were all that).

cases.name: order-hub-acl-echoes-could-not-resolve-filename
cases.input:
remote: REJECTED: notes/could not resolve.md out of scope
 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined)
cases.why: the hub echoes the offending FILEPATH onto its `remote:` line and `remote` is a transport producer prefix on both sides, so _is_network_error genuinely matches 'could not resolve' here — network is true, and that is a fact about the predicate rather than a bug in it. The verdict is still ACL because both classifiers test the refusal branches BEFORE transport, so ordering is the only thing keeping the answer right and this case is what pins it (#535/#584/#617).

 ! [remote rejected] main -> main (pre-receive hook declined)
cases.why: the hub echoes the offending FILEPATH onto its `remote:` line and `remote` is a transport producer prefix on both sides, so _is_network_error genuinely matches 'no route to host' here — network is true, and that is a fact about the predicate rather than a bug in it. The verdict is still ACL because both classifiers test the refusal branches BEFORE transport, so ordering is the only thing keeping the answer right and this case is what pins it (#535/#584/#617).

cases.name: own-detail-wrapped-connect-refused
cases.input:
Hub unreachable — changes saved locally. Push when network available.
  Detail: ssh: connect to host 127.0.0.1 port 1: Connection refused
fatal: Could not read from remote repository.
cases.why: sync_push/sync_pull print the CLI's own network banner, then `f"  Detail: {output}"` on the next line — wrapping ONLY output's first line and breaking the producer anchor on it (the `ssh:` token no longer starts the line). This is exactly what a live push against a refusing/dead hub writes to `.schist/last-sync-error`, and what a downstream re-classification of that captured text (MCP's classifyPushFailure) has to read, since _is_network_error/_TRANSPORT_PRODUCER_LINE_RE only see the raw pre-wrap output at the point sync.py calls them. Without tolerating this literal `Detail:` lead, this real scenario fell through to `other`, which #531's write-gate fails closed on — silently keeping the exact deadlock the gate exists to clear.

cases.name: steer-detail-wrapped-bare-filename-no-producer-token
cases.input:
error: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by rebase:
	Detail: connection refused.md
cases.why: the `Detail:` tolerance added for own-detail-wrapped-connect-refused still requires a producer TOKEN (ssh/curl/fatal/remote/…) to immediately follow it. A vault file literally named `Detail: connection refused.md`, echoed by git's own local conflict-hint block, supplies `Detail:` and the transport PHRASE 'connection refused' but no producer token — so it does not match, proving the tolerance doesn't reopen filename-steering (#535/#584/#617's risk class, not a new one).
